body.statement:
For every sufficiently small \(\delta>0\), let
\(h\asymp\delta^{1/\gamma}\) and
\(\ell\asymp\delta^{1/q}\).  There is a sufficiently small constant
\(c_0>0\), depending only on \(d\), such that, if \(n\ell^d\le c_0\),
there are two priors on
laws in \(\mathcal M_H\), one supported on \(\theta(P)=\delta\) and the
other on \(\theta(P)=0\), such that their one-record prior predictives are
identical, their \(n\)-record prior predictives admit a coupling with
\[
 \mathbb E d_{\mathrm{Ham}}(D_n,D_n')
 \le C\delta n^2h^d\ell^d,
\]
and their squared Hellinger distance is at most
\(C n^2\delta^2h^d\ell^d\).  The constants depend only on
\(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,e_0\).
body.proof_tex:
We give the construction explicitly.  Let \(g_h\) be a smooth bump supported
in a side-\(h\) cube about \(x_0\), with \(g_h(x_0)=1\), and put
\(G_h=g_h^2\).  If \(\eta\) is a fixed smooth bump whose lattice translates
cover \(\mathbb R^d\), define the quadratic partition
\[
 w_j(x)=\frac{\eta((x-z_j)/\ell)}
 {\{\sum_m\eta((x-z_m)/\ell)^2\}^{1/2}},\qquad
 \phi_j=g_hw_j.
\]
The denominator is uniformly positive, overlap is bounded, and hence
\(\sum_j\phi_j^2=G_h\) and
\(\|\phi_j\|_{\mathcal H^s}\le C\ell^{-s}\).  For independent Rademacher
signs \(\lambda_j\), let \(f_\lambda=\sum_j\lambda_j\phi_j\).  Then
\(\mathbb E_\lambda f_\lambda=0\) and
\(\mathbb E_\lambda f_\lambda^2=G_h\).

Choose \(a=c\ell^\alpha\), \(b=c\ell^\beta\), and \(\delta=4ab\), adjusting
fixed scale constants so that \(h\asymp\delta^{1/\gamma}\).  When
\(\alpha\ge\beta\), use
\[
 (\pi_P,\mu_{0,P},\tau_P)
 =(1/2,1/2+bf_\lambda-\delta G_h/2,\delta G_h),
 \quad
 (\pi_Q,\mu_{0,Q},\tau_Q)
 =(1/2+af_\lambda,1/2+bf_\lambda,0).
\]
When \(\beta>\alpha\), use
\[
 (\pi_P,\mu_{0,P},\tau_P)
 =(1/2+af_\lambda,1/2-\delta G_h/2,\delta G_h),
 \quad
 (\pi_Q,\mu_{0,Q},\tau_Q)
 =(1/2+af_\lambda,1/2+bf_\lambda,0).
\]
Let \(X\) be uniform, let \(Y\in\{0,1\}\) conditionally have the displayed
regression, and construct potential outcomes conditionally independently of
\(A\) before imposing consistency.  Scaled smoothness, \(q<\gamma\), and a
sufficiently small fixed \(c\) put all these laws in \(\mathcal M_H\) and
keep propensities and regressions in \([1/4,3/4]\).

With \(s=2A-1\) and \(z=2Y-1\), four times the conditional masses in the
first case are
\[
 p_\lambda=1+2zbf_\lambda+sz\delta G_h,\qquad
 q_\lambda=1+2saf_\lambda+2zbf_\lambda+4szabf_\lambda^2,
\]
and in the second case they are
\[
 p_\lambda=1+2saf_\lambda+sz\delta G_h+2za\delta f_\lambda G_h,
 \qquad
 q_\lambda=1+2saf_\lambda+2zbf_\lambda+4szabf_\lambda^2.
\]
The two Rademacher moment identities and \(4ab=\delta\) prove equality of
the one-record mixtures.

Condition on all covariates and join two record indices when their active
\(\phi_j\)'s overlap.  Different graph components use independent signs.
For a component of size \(m\), expand its product masses and average the
signs.  The degree-zero and degree-one terms cancel.  Every remaining
difference contains \(\delta\), \(ab=\delta/4\), or two copies of the
nuisance amplitude absent from one fiber.  That last amplitude is \(a\) if
\(\alpha\ge\beta\) and \(b\) otherwise, and respectively
\(a^2\le ab\) or \(b^2\le ab\).  Choosing the first two involved record
positions and summing all residual factors by the binomial theorem gives
\[
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\overline P_m,\overline Q_m)
 \le C\delta(m)_2(1+c)^m. \tag{4}
\]
For each finite component law, put the pointwise minimum of the two masses
on the diagonal and couple the residual masses arbitrarily.  Its failure
probability is the total variation in (4); replace all \(m\) records on a
failure.  A collision neighborhood count is dominated by
\(1+\operatorname{Bin}(n-1,C\ell^d)\); its required exponentially weighted
moments are bounded when \(n\ell^d\le c_0\); smallness of \(c_0\) makes the
bounded-degree component exploration subcritical.  There are at most \(Cnh^d\)
records in the macro support in expectation, and each has collision
probability at most \(Cn\ell^d\).  Equation (4) therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb E d_{\mathrm{Ham}}(D_n,D_n')
 \le C\delta n^2h^d\ell^d.
\]
For Hellinger distance, square the component likelihood difference before
summing.  Equality of the one-record mixtures again makes a collision
necessary, while (4)'s first nonzero coefficient has magnitude at most
\(C\delta\).  The same collision count and exponential-moment calculation
gives
\[
 H^2\!\left(\int P_\lambda^{\otimes n}d\varpi,
              \int Q_\lambda^{\otimes n}d\varpi\right)
 \le Cn^2\delta^2h^d\ell^d.
\]
This proves every claimed property from the displayed construction.
